newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Arafat heads for U.S. with "bag full of promises".
newsitem.headline: Arafat heads for U.S. with "bag full of promises".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat left for Washington on Tuesday promising to attend a Middle East peace summit later in the day with an open mind and a commitment to peace.
"Our bags are not empty ... our bags are full of promises and desires," Arafat told a news conference after a meeting with a group of European Union foreign ministers on Monday evening.

The PLO leader -- sticking to a punishing schedule that saw him in Jerusalem on Monday morning, Egypt at midday and Luxembourg in the evening -- left shortly after midnight (2200 GMT) to attend a peace summit called by President Bill Clinton.

Clinton called the summit following a week of violence sparked by an Israeli decision to open a pedestrian tunnel to archaeological sites by Jerusalem's Temple Mount, sacred to both Judaism and Islam.

Arafat, speaking after meeting the EU's so-called troika -- a group made up of the past, current and future foreign ministers of the 15-nation bloc -- said he would attend the summit with "no conditions or ultimatums".

But he stressed that the Israeli government could make a great gesture towards calming the situation by closing the tunnel as well as speeding up the withdrawal of settlers from the West Bank town of Hebron.

Foreign Minister Dick Spring of Ireland -- the current EU president -- said the troika had promised continued financial and other aid to Palestinian authorities and called on Israel to show "a strong signal that they are committed to peace".
He said he would contact U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to brief him on the outcome of the EU's talks with Arafat.
The European Union (EU), miffed at being frozen out of the peace process, invited Arafat here ahead of a regular meeting of the bloc's foreign ministers scheduled for Tuesday.
The EU is the biggest financial supporter of the Palestinian authority, although Arafat said the closure of the border with Israel was costing his country "$6 million to $7 million a day".
Arafat said 84 Palestinians had been killed and over 1,600 others wounded in clashes with Israeli troops since fighting began. Fourteen Israelis are reported to have been killed in fighting.

He told reporters not to read too much into the absence of Hosni Mubarak from the summit, saying the Egyptian president had urged him to attend and had ordered his foreign minister, Amr Moussa, to assist.
Mubarak had wanted to postpone the summit pending assurances it would bring firm guarantees of Israeli gestures toward the Palestinians.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and King Hussein of Jordan will also attend.
Arafat told reporters that he was comitted to getting an agreement from the summit, adding: "We are going there to push forward the peace process and to achieve something concrete.
"Peace is a precious target," he added.
